subject: Discovery recap and next steps — Redwood + Acme Enterprise
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap and next steps — Redwood + Acme Enterprise

Alex — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our call so we have alignment and clear next steps.

Meeting summary / pain points we heard:
- Latency variability on peak traffic (p95 spikes impacting UX during campaigns).
- High unit cost and poor predictability running inference across mixed GPU fleet.
- Challenges with cold-starts / KV cache warm-up for multi-tenant inference flows.
- Security/compliance requirement: customer data must remain in Acme-controlled VPC and we need audit logs & KMS integration.

Current stack (what you told us):
- On-prem GPU pool (NVIDIA A100 + mixed older nodes) managed by your infra team.
- In-house inference runtime for a subset of features; some traffic routed through a managed provider for burst.
- Observability via internal Prometheus/Grafana; limited token-level cost visibility.

Success criteria you outlined:
- p95 inference latency for interactive features <= 150ms in target workload.
- Unit-cost goals: reduce per-token inference charge by ~30% vs current managed provider run-rate (we can refine with usage).
- Ability to run in a VPC/on-prem footprint with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and 12-month audit retention.

Immediate next steps / asks from our side:
1) Please share the stakeholder list & decision process (procurement, legal, SRE, CTO) and target timeline for a procurement decision.
2) Intro to procurement & security (if you can loop them in, that will speed timeline).
3) We’ll provide a short POC plan + commercial guardrails for review (attached: POC-Plan.xlsx and Redwood-Product-Overview.pdf).

Procurement framing (initial commercial guardrails to accelerate evaluation):
- Pilot: 3-month POC covering representative workload (we recommend reserved pilot capacity equal to your 95th percentile during baseline windows).
- Commercial: heads-of-terms with a 6-month reserved option OR month-to-month usage pricing for hosted with a clear overage policy.
- Budget expectations: we’ll provide a ballpark estimate once we get a rough monthly token/GPU profile — this avoids misaligned expectations in procurement.

Proposed times for a short triage call next week (30 minutes): Thu 6/4 10–11am PT or Fri 6/5 9–11am PT. Let me know what works and I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — happy to jump on a joint call with Rishi and Vivek for the procurement convo.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0123

[Attachments: Redwood-Product-Overview.pdf (PDF), POC-Plan.xlsx (Excel)]

To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Emily Park <emily.park@acme.com>, Ben Thomson <ben.thomson@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap and next steps — Redwood + Acme Enterprise

Emily / Ben — thanks for joining the thread. Quick procurement framing to make the next few weeks productive: 

1) Decision process & stakeholders we typically see:
   - Procurement/Legal (Emily/Ben) — T&Cs, DPA, commercial terms.
   - Infrastructure/SRE (Sara Miller/CTO team) — technical fit & on-prem/VPC requirements.
   - Product/PD (Alex) — success criteria and UX validation.

2) Typical timeline for a pilot -> procurement (examples):
   - Week 0: POC kickoff (3-week technical validation recommended).
   - Week 3–6: Evaluation & integration items, security review.
   - Week 6–8: Commercial negotiation and contract execution (can be faster with standard terms).

3) Initial commercial guardrails (so procurement has context):
   - Pilot scope: 3 months; we can size pilot to your traffic profile and agree on a capped pilot spend.
   - Pricing constructs: reserved capacity (monthly commit) OR usage-based with monthly reconciliation.
   - Ballpark: for budgeting conversations only, a pilot sized for ~100K tokens/day across mixed interactive & batch traffic typically maps to a low 5-figure monthly pilot spend; we will refine with exact traffic profile.

4) Artifacts we’ll provide this week:
   - POC plan (attached).
   - Draft SLA / heads-of-terms (attached: SLA_Draft.docx).
   - SOC2 & security posture summary (we’ll send the SOC2 PDF and DPA via secure link once you confirm recipients).

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa to share the full POC plan, draft SLA, and a simple SOW for the pilot (today).
- Procurement to confirm required artifacts and any preferred contract redlines (Emily).
- Schedule a 30-min commercial call with procurement + engineering next week.

Preferred times for a call: Thu 6/4 10am PT (I can do an intro call then) or Fri 6/5 10am PT. If neither works, suggest two windows that do.

Thanks — looping Rishi to capture technical follow-ups in the POC doc.

Best,
Marissa

[Attachments: SLA_Draft.docx (Word)]

Subject: Re: Discovery recap and next steps — Redwood + Acme Enterprise

Hi Marissa / Alex — thanks for the clear framing. Procurement side — initial asks and timeline: 

1) Artifacts we need to start (please attach or share secure links):
   - SOC 2 Type II report (or expected delivery date)
   - Standard DPA and sample contract (redline-friendly)
   - Ballpark heads-of-terms / commercial estimate for a 3-month pilot (we understand this is indicative)

2) Stakeholders & timeline:
   - Procurement: Emily Park (me) — will lead commercial review.
   - Legal: Ben Thomson — contract review & redlines.
   - Technical: Sara Miller (CTO) — infra/security review.
   - Expected procurement cadence: 4–8 weeks from pilot sign-off to PO depending on security review outcomes.

3) PoC success criteria we will evaluate: alignment to p95 latency target, integration effort (time to inference), and clear rollback/exit terms.

4) Please also include any documentation on data residency, KMS integrations, and audit log retention.

If you can share the SOC2 + DPA and a quick pilot cost estimate by end of day Monday, we’ll schedule a short procurement call (30m) with Legal & Technical next week.

Best,
Emily Park
Senior Procurement Manager — Acme Enterprise
emily.park@acme.com
